“You look awful,” Eshaan said, dropping his bag next to Sarika in the corridor.
“Two nights. Don't start.”
“Two nights of what?”
“Deliveries. After ten. A man from a group chat offered it, no forms, no questions. Easy money.”
“And the maths test you slept through?”
“It's one test.”
“What was in the bags?”
Sarika looked at the floor. “He said not to open them.”
“Did he pay you?”
“Friday. He promised.”
“Last night, what happened?”
“A car kept slowing beside me. I dumped the bags at the tea stall and ran.” Her hands were shaking now.
“Then he's not paying you Friday. Come on, we're telling the counsellor. Right now.”
Sarika nodded. At the office the counsellor looked up, saw her face and said, “Sit down. You're not in trouble.”

What might Sarika be feeling as she describes the car?
qa.a: Fear: her hands are shaking as she admits she ran, which shows the easy money no longer feels safe.

qa.q: What should Sarika have done before accepting, and why?
qa.a: She should have asked who the man was, what was in the bags and the exact hours, and told a parent or teacher first, because vague terms and night work for a school student are warning signs.

qa.q: How does the job look to Eshaan?
qa.a: Eshaan sees a stranger handing a schoolmate unknown bags at night, so he worries about her safety and wants a trusted adult involved straight away.

grounding: A student takes a night delivery job with vague terms, and it proves unsafe and clashes with school.

Last winter I took the first job anyone offered me. I'm Tushar, and I was fifteen and desperate for money for a new cricket bat.

A man I'd never met messaged me after seeing my post in a local group. "Food deliveries on your cycle. Nine to one at night. Cash daily. No papers needed." It sounded easy. I didn't ask who he was, or what the rules were for someone my age. I didn't tell my parents; I said I was studying at Lalremsiami's.

The first night I rode alone through dark lanes near the highway. At midnight two men on a bike followed me for a whole street. I was shaking. The next morning I fell asleep in the first period, and the teacher sent me to the office.

That afternoon I told my father everything. He called the number, told the man I was a minor and wouldn't be coming, and blocked it.

qa.q: What hours did the delivery job involve?
How did Tushar feel when the two men followed on the bike?
qa.a: Tushar felt terrified, shaking as they followed for a whole street.

qa.q: What should Tushar have checked before accepting the job?
qa.a: Who the man was, whether night work is even allowed at that age, and whether it clashed with school, and Tushar should have talked to a parent first.

qa.q: How might Tushar's father have felt hearing the story?
qa.a: He was probably frightened and angry at the stranger, but acted calmly and quickly by ending the arrangement the same day.

grounding: A reflective account of a teen accepting a vague night delivery job from a stranger that looks easy but is unsafe, likely illegal for a minor and clashes with school.

Class teacher's note, Class 10B

For a week Rafiq came in pale, yawning through first period. On Thursday he put his head on the desk and fell asleep during the test.

I asked him to stay back. After some hesitation, he told me that a man he met at the bus stand had offered him delivery work, carrying parcels on a scooter from 10 pm to 2 am. Cash, no questions. He did not know what was in the parcels. His friend Anirban had warned him, but he had said the money was too good.

I told Rafiq he had done the right thing by telling me and that he was not in trouble with me. I explained that night work of this kind is not allowed for someone his age and could be unsafe. I phoned his mother before he left school that afternoon, and she came in. He has agreed not to return to the job. I have informed the principal.

qa.q: What were the hours of Rafiq's delivery work?
How might Rafiq have felt when asked to stay back?
qa.a: He probably felt anxious and ashamed, hesitating before explaining the job.

qa.q: What better choice could Rafiq have made when the offer came?
qa.a: He could have asked his parents or a teacher before saying yes, and looked for daytime work that is allowed for his age.

qa.q: How might Anirban see the outcome?
qa.a: Anirban would likely feel relieved and a little vindicated, since the warning about the job turned out to be right.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a teen who took a vague night delivery job from a stranger, which was unsafe, unsuitable for a minor and clashed with school.
